title: FIXTURE: The Harbor Bridge Closure

question.prompt: The city council is to blame for the harbor bridge closing.

starting_facts.text: The fictional Harbor Bridge closed to traffic on 2026-08-01 after an inspection report.
The city council controls the bridge maintenance budget.

steps.headline: Inspectors rated the deck 'poor' in 2023.
steps.body: A 2023 inspection gave the bridge deck a poor rating. The report recommended repairs within two years. This is a fictional test fixture.

depth.title: 2023 inspection report
depth.summary: The report lists cracking in three deck panels and recommends repair.

micro_poll.statement: The city should have fixed the bridge right after this report.

steps.headline: The council voted twice to delay repair funding.
steps.body: Minutes show the council postponed the repair line item in 2024 and 2025. Both votes passed 5 to 4. This is a fictional test fixture.

micro_poll.statement: The council was wrong to delay the repair money.

steps.headline: The state cut its bridge grant by 40% in 2024.
steps.body: The state transportation agency reduced local bridge grants in 2024. The city's share fell by 40 percent. This is a fictional test fixture.

depth.text: We had to choose between the bridge and the school roof.
depth.speaker: A council member

micro_poll.statement: The state cut is a fair excuse for the delay.

steps.headline: A contractor says the 2025 crack was new and sudden.
steps.body: The repair contractor told a local paper the crack that forced the closure appeared within weeks. The city engineer has not confirmed this. This is a fictional test fixture.

depth.title: Why sudden cracks matter
depth.body: If the failure was sudden, earlier repairs might not have prevented it.

micro_poll.statement: A sudden new crack means no one could have seen this coming.

sides.label: The council is responsible
sides.steelman: The council was warned in 2023 and chose to delay repairs twice.

sides.label: The council is not responsible
sides.steelman: State cuts forced hard choices, and the failure that closed the bridge may have been sudden.

open_questions: Would the 2023 repairs have prevented the 2025 crack?
What will the state do with next year's grants?

sources.title: Viral post about the bridge closure

takes.label: How the left is telling it
takes.summary: The state starved the city of money, and now people blame the council for a crack nobody could see. This is a fictional test fixture.

checks.claim: The state cut the bridge grant.
checks.note: The state cut the grant by 40% in 2024.

takes.label: How the middle is telling it
takes.summary: Everyone had a part: the council delayed, and the state cut money. This is a fictional test fixture.

checks.claim: The council delayed the repair money twice.
checks.note: The meeting minutes show two votes to delay.

takes.label: How the right is telling it
takes.summary: The council wasted two years after a clear warning. This is a fictional test fixture.

checks.note: The council knew of the poor rating but voted to delay, not to ignore it.
